validity.researcher_notes: The row's own wiki cites only OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (p.75) and 2017 (p.136) — country-level gas-pipeline total tables that do NOT name this line, its endpoints, length, or diameter. They cannot corroborate a single 56 km segment. The name itself, 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56', is a kilometer-post segment label (km0 to km56 of a line 'UBTG-1'), i.e. a GIS/OSM digitizing artifact rather than an operator or media name. Every independent web hit for 'UBTG-1' or 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56' resolves back to gem.wiki (this row and its siblings); no Aramco release, MEED, Argaam, Saudi Gazette, Arab News, or trade source names 'UBTG-1'. Endpoints in the sheet are placeholder 'Saudi Arabia' -> 'Saudi Arabia'. The underlying PHYSICAL corridor is real: this sits inside Aramco's Master Gas System in the Eastern Province (Ghawar / Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah-Berri gas-plant complex) — the MEED Hawiyah-pipeline-programme article documents Aramco's '-1' line-code convention (HDUG-1 = Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line, HUG-1 = Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah gas line), so 'UBTG-1' is plausibly an analogous Aramco route code, and trade coverage describes a 56" rich-gas line Hawiyah->Uthmaniyah (matches sibling P1912). But the SPECIFIC named row P1910 has no independent attestation. Not a phantom corridor, but an unverifiable, un-named GIS segment — meets the existence-concern bar (only cited source doesn't name it; all independent traces are GEM-derived).

routes.corridor_desc: Segment lies within Aramco's Master Gas System in the Eastern Province, inside/around the Ghawar complex. Direction inferred from the sibling chain: P1912 runs Hawiyah Gas Plant (~24.80N, 49.39E) -> UBTG-1 km0; P1910/P1911 run km0 -> km56; P1900 continues km56 -> AY-1 KP916 (the A47-Yanbu trunk). So km0 sits ~56 km from Hawiyah in the Hawiyah/Uthmaniyah gas-plant belt, and km56 lies ~56 km further along the trunk toward Berri/Juaymah and the AY-1 line, trending generally north from the Hawiyah area. This is a LOOSE corridor bound (KP markers km0/km56 are not surveyable named facilities); tightest defensible box is the Eastern Province Ghawar-to-Berri MGS corridor, roughly 24.8-27.0N / 49.3-49.9E. Endpoint coordinates left null to avoid fabrication; only the Hawiyah plant anchor is a real public location.
